correctness.rationale: For n>=3, every 3-bit column is encoded and the all-vertex MM stability condition is precisely at least two agreeing neighbors among four. The 64x64 transfer trace counts each labeled cyclic configuration once. The fully specified integer matrix yields the stated factorization from a successful exact SymPy characteristic-polynomial computation; Rouché inequalities isolate the unique simple eigenvalue 3. For RMM, a minority bit in a mixed three-bit column can have at most two matching neighbors, hence every absorbing singleton has monochromatic columns; the 4x4 no-isolated-bit transfer matrix has characteristic (z^2-z-1)(z^2-z+1). Independent vertex-neighbor brute force for n=3,4,5,6 agrees. Exact algebra plus bijections, not the finite tests, cover all n.

value.rationale: The width-three torus is the smallest graph in the natural 4-regular two-dimensional torus family, and counting stable colorings under two standard tie conventions measures precisely how the 1D cycle dichotomy changes under transverse coupling. The new 3 versus golden-ratio exponential rates give exact asymptotic fixed-point entropies and testable finite benchmarks, not a merely routine single-configuration example. Exact characterization of all widths remains unproved.
